transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Hurst.
With days to go to the midterm election Tuesday,
candidates are out on the trail rallying supporters to go out and vote.
In Texas, Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton...
This isn't just red versus blue.
It's the America our founders gave us versus something they would never recognize.
...and his opponent, Democrat James Tellerico...
We are running against the most corrupt politician in Texas.
Ken Paxton represents everything that's wrong with our politics.
He doesn't serve us. He serves himself.
The both made closing arguments yesterday in a toss-up Senate race
that's become a measure of voter frustrations with President Trump's leadership.
In Michigan, the Senate race between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed
and Republican Mike Rogers is another of this year's most competitive contests.
President Trump, meanwhile, is back on the campaign trail today,
visiting Iowa and Kansas after initially canceling those rallies.
Trump also says he has events planned tomorrow without saying what those are.
In the German city of Frankfurt, hooded rioters looted stores last night
and clashed with police.
As Esme Nicholson reports, the violence followed a day of mainly peaceful,
youth-led protests across the country.
Thousands of young people took to the streets of 34 cities across Germany
to demand better prospects,
instead of what they view as an uncertain and unaffordable future.
The protests were organized by Gen Z Regelt, or Gen Z Takes Charge,
a group of school and university students asking for a better education
instead of the reintroduction of military service.
Most demonstrations were non-violent,
but police reported disturbances in Cologne, Hamburg and Bremen.
And in Frankfurt, police sealed off a major shopping avenue
as violent looters targeted stores, including a firearms shop.
Frankfurt authorities suspect extremists instigated the violence.
For NPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson in Berlin.
The Golden State Valkyries are the new WNBA champs
after a tight game against the Atlanta Dream yesterday.
Natalia Navarro with member station KQED has more.
This is the Valkyries' second season in existence,
and their finals win is the fastest any expansion franchise
has won a championship in six decades
across all major North American professional sports leagues.
I'm so elated.
I've never felt like this in San Francisco.
This is the best thing in San Francisco that's ever happened.
That's Tana Kissinger, one of the more than 18,000 fans
sporting violet and Halloween costumes that packed Chase Center,
also known as Ball Hala.
Throughout the season, fans' positivity and inclusiveness
have defined the community around the team.
And the party is just getting started.
The victory parade is scheduled for this Wednesday.
For NPR News, I'm Natalia Navarro in San Francisco.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Researchers have been tracking bird flu around the globe,
most recently jumping from Antarctica to Australia.
Millions of poultry and wild animals have died from it.
But NPR's Gabriela Emanuel reports,
researchers have discovered that one of the big die-offs in Antarctica
was actually caused by another disease.
When Ralph Vinstriels sailed to the Danger Islands
just off the Antarctic Peninsula,
his team of researchers found penguin carcasses all over.
They took samples expecting to find the bird flu virus.
And their result was, yes, there is bird flu here,
but the virus loads aren't low.
And that was a little bit puzzling.
Vinstriels is a wildlife veterinarian at the University of California, Davis.
It turns out most of the birds died from avian cholera,
which does not pose a major risk to humans.
However, the strain they found is very similar
to one found 5,000 miles away on an island in the southern Indian Ocean.
He says it just shows how connected Antarctica is to the rest of the world.
And how scientists need to keep close watch
on the pathogens circulating there.
Gabriela Emanuel, NPR News.
On Wall Street this week,
tech companies are coming off a steep sell-off
after the NASDAQ lost about 2% on Friday.
Apple will release its latest earnings tomorrow,
and though it's a smaller player in the AI space
compared to other tech giants,
investors will focus on the company's information on supply issues
as the price of memory chips rise, leading Apple to raise prices.
I'm Janine Herbst, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
See photos of past work, and request and compare quotes
to find your best price, all in one place.
Download the free Angie app today or visit Angie.com.
That's A-N-G-I dot com.

topics.text: Texas Senate candidates Ken Paxton and James Tellerico make closing arguments before midterm election
Michigan Senate race between Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers highlighted as competitive contest
President Trump resumes campaign rallies in Iowa and Kansas after initially canceling them
Frankfurt rioters loot stores and clash with police after youth-led protests across Germany
Golden State Valkyries win WNBA championship over Atlanta Dream in tight final game
Researchers find avian cholera, not bird flu, caused major penguin die-off on Danger Islands
Apple to release earnings; investors watch supply issues and rising memory chip prices
